boundary: Successive control regimes are distinct layers, never one network. Regimes may overlap in time because they govern different domains (ranch land, the track site, water, downtown planning, private assembly); they are never collapsed into a single timeless graph.

regimes.label: Tongva landscape (Alyeupkigna)
regimes.control_description: Tongva village at the base of Little Santa Anita Canyon within the spring-fed alluvial-fan landscape. Start date is widened, not known: documented occupation predates the European record; 1771 marks the founding of Mission San Gabriel.

regimes.label: Mission and rancho land control
regimes.control_description: Mission San Gabriel control of the rancheria (agricultural outpost from 1800), then the Mexican grant of Rancho Santa Anita (Hugo Reid, formalized 1845) and its Anglo-era ownership chain through Newmark.

regimes.label: Baldwin consolidated control (foundational land/water/rail/townsite)
regimes.control_description: One owner simultaneously held the ranch land, its creek/spring/lake water endowment, the rail right-of-way and depot sites (as railroad stockholder), the incorporated townsite (first mayor, 1903), the liquor licensing, and the 1907 racetrack. The only era in which one person occupied every control layer at once.

regimes.label: Inheritance and subdivision
regimes.control_description: Anita Baldwin's inheritance (1909-1936), the 1936 sale to a Chandler-family syndicate, subdivision through 1947, and county flood-control infrastructure (Santa Anita Dam 1927) replacing private water control.

regimes.label: Racetrack construction and private operation
regimes.control_description: Los Angeles Turf Club (Strub/Roach; architect Kaufmann) buys 214 acres from Anita Baldwin and opens Santa Anita Park (1934-12-25) after Proposition 5 (1933) legalizes pari-mutuel wagering; operation passes through Meditrust (1997) to the Magna/Stronach lineage (1998) to The Stronach Group / 1/ST. Track pari-mutuel revenue funds the city's Capital Outlay Fund.

regimes.label: Wartime federal control
regimes.control_description: WCCA Santa Anita Assembly Center (1942-03-27 to 1942-10-27; peak 18,719 incarcerated Japanese Americans), then U.S. Army Camp Santa Anita ordnance training (to December 1944); racing resumed May 1945.

regimes.label: Postwar suburbanization and adjudicated water
regimes.control_description: Raymond Basin adjudication (judgment 1944-12-23, California's first) replaces open pumping with watermaster governance; population more than doubles 1940-1950; from the 1970s the San Gabriel Valley's demographic and real-estate transformation (Hsieh-era marketing to Chinese buyers) reshapes demand.

regimes.label: Redevelopment and rail planning
regimes.control_description: Arcadia Redevelopment Agency (1968) and the Central Redevelopment Project Area (1973, amended 2007) run tax-increment value capture; the Downtown 2000 program reconstructs Huntington and First (streetscape, water system, 28 facades) before 2010; Measure R (2008) funds the Gold Line Phase 2A; the 2010 General Plan designates Downtown Mixed-Use around a station explicitly planned at First/Santa Clara; redevelopment dissolves statewide 2012-02-01.

regimes.label: Downtown association / assessment-district era
regimes.control_description: City-initiated Community Benefits District effort (authorized 2012-05-15, consultant New City America, $70,000 per city council minutes) targeting completion before the station opening; no enabling resolution establishing an assessment district was located in city clerk records sampled for 2012-2016. The Downtown Arcadia Improvement Association forms 2013 as a 501(c)(3) (FY2025 revenue $160,121, ~96% contributions); Erik Wahl serves as an officer from 2020 (1st VP 2020-2021, President 2022-2025). City support since 2023 runs through discretionary per-event sponsorship resolutions (Resolution 7497, $20,000 for the 2023 Patriotic Festival) formalized as a Community Events Sponsorship Policy by Resolution 7629 (2025-05-20) — an operational, non-statutory relationship.

regimes.label: Transit activation
regimes.control_description: Gold Line Phase 2A passenger service from 2016-03-05; Arcadia station at First/Santa Clara with a 300-space structure, fully Measure R-funded, reported at nearly $1 billion for the six-station segment. The parking structure and transit plaza were multi-agency funded (City of Arcadia, Construction Authority/Metro, and an FTA grant); the city separately issued Series 2011 GO bonds ($7.22M outstanding in 2015) for the Santa Anita Avenue grade separation. Metro operates the corridor and, as of retrieval, lists no joint-development site at Arcadia; the station becomes the fixed point around which downtown land value re-prices.

regimes.label: Property acquisition and parcel assembly (documented era)
regimes.control_description: The deed chronology is now resolved for the one site with a documentable chain: Positive Investments bought the Alexan Azalea block on 2018-01-24 for $25.6M, about 22 months after the 2016-03-05 opening, not before. Every other target-site reassessment (57 Wheeler construction 2017; Arroyo 2019; Derby 2020; Town Center partial-interest 2024/2026; Azalea development parcels 2024, matching the TCR/Positive JV purchase) likewise postdates the opening. No retrieved public record shows any current player holding these parcels before the station opened; the 2024 JV deed's named seller remains unresolved after search.

regimes.label: Entitlement and construction
regimes.control_description: Development Code (Ord. 2341, comprehensive update reported November 2016; DMU 60 ft / 80 du/acre), Housing Element (2022) and 2024 rezonings expand downtown capacity; Alexan Azalea approved 2022-07-21, Derby 2023-12-19, Arcadia Town Center 2025-01-14; Le Meridien opens 2021.

regimes.label: Present street reconstruction
regimes.control_description: FY2026-31 CIP arterial pavement rehabilitation of First Avenue (Huntington to Duarte): grind-and-overlay plus curbs, ramps, sidewalks, and pedestrian bulb-outs, Prop C/STPL-exchange funded, bid March 2026; ARPA-funded Downtown Lighting and Streetscape ($225,000: palm-tree uplighting, a First Avenue banner installation, and planter/signage refresh), with an August 2025 $247,000 contract award for the lighting work. The city's 'First Avenue Corridor Improvements' webpage remains an unpopulated stub distinct from both funded projects; the earlier full utility/streetscape rebuild of First was the Downtown 2000 era, not this project.

regimes.label: Comparable corridors (Monrovia, Duarte, Crenshaw/K Line)
regimes.control_description: A distinct, non-Arcadia layer held for control purposes: Old Town Monrovia's business-license BID and merchant advisory board; the Crenshaw corridor's property-based BID (established 2002-12-18, predating the K Line by two decades) and the 2021 Harridge assembly of Baldwin Hills Crenshaw Plaza; and Duarte's 2013 Station Specific Plan (rooted in an August 2007 General Plan re-designation), amended 2019, delivered by MBK Rental Living and Jamboree Housing. These regimes never join Arcadia's control chain; they exist to test whether Arcadia's formation is distinctive or the default SoCal corridor shape.
